mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% over the last three months indicates a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP by more than 2% over the last quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer confidence rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of instances with strong GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% over the last month indicates a surge in supply-side activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in real estate sales (RSAFS) exceeds 10%, it signals a strong demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS YoY growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the last month, it signals strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) inflation rate by more than 1%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and real GDP (GDPC1) both increase by more than 2% over the last quarter, it signals a robust economic expansion, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and corporate earnings improve.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 increase > 2% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect between HOUST and GDPC1 on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
